subject: Islamic Studies
q: Abu Sufyan accepted Islam at the time of:
explanation: Abu Sufyan, the Quraysh leader, embraced Islam as the Muslim army approached Makkah in 8 AH.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Uthman (RA) did not take part in the Battle of Badr because of:
explanation: The Prophet told him to stay in Madinah to nurse his wife Ruqayyah, the Prophet’s daughter, who died during the battle; he was counted among the people of Badr.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which woman Companion fought to defend the Holy Prophet (PBUH) at the Battle of Uhud?
explanation: Nusaybah (Umm Ammarah) came to give water but took up arms and shielded the Prophet when the lines broke.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Rufaidah Al-Aslamiyyah (RA) is remembered in Islamic history as:
o: The first woman to memorise the Qur’an
The first woman to migrate to Abyssinia
explanation: Rufaidah set up a tent beside the Prophet’s Mosque to treat the wounded and trained other women in nursing.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Asma bint Abi Bakr (RA) is known as “Zat-un-Nitaqain” because she:
o: Wore two veils at the Battle of Yarmuk
Nursed two wounded soldiers at Uhud
Tore her waistband in two to tie provisions for the Hijrah
explanation: She split her waistband to tie the food and water bags for the Prophet and Abu Bakr on the Hijrah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Abu Ubaidah bin al-Jarrah (RA), commander in Syria, died in the:
explanation: Abu Ubaidah refused to leave his troops during the plague of Amwas in 18 AH and died of it.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Uthman (RA) bought the well of Rumah in Madinah in order to:
o: Supply water to his own orchards
Make its water free for all Muslims
explanation: Madinah was short of sweet water; Uthman bought Bir Rumah from its owner and endowed it for public use.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which Companion made a very large contribution towards equipping the army of Tabuk?
explanation: Uthman provided camels, horses and money for Jaish-ul-Usrah, and the Prophet prayed for him.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Who was the first caliph of the Umayyad dynasty?
explanation: Muawiyah bin Abi Sufyan founded Umayyad rule in 41 AH with Damascus as his capital.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The year 41 AH, when Hazrat Hasan (RA) transferred the caliphate to Hazrat Muawiyah (RA), is called:
explanation: It is called the Year of Unity because the Muslims were reunited under one ruler after years of civil strife.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The tragedy of Karbala, in which Hazrat Imam Husain (RA) was martyred, took place in:
explanation: Husain (RA) and members of his family were martyred at Karbala in Iraq on 10 Muharram 61 AH.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which Umayyad ruler is often called the fifth rightly guided caliph?
explanation: His brief reign was remembered for justice, simplicity and reform in the spirit of the Rashidun.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: What was the real name of Imam Abu Hanifa?
explanation: Imam Abu Hanifa, founder of the Hanafi school, was named Nu’man bin Thabit; Abu Hanifa was his kunyah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Imam Malik bin Anas lived and taught in:
explanation: Imam Malik spent his life in Madinah and based his school on the practice of its people.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which Imam was imprisoned and flogged during the Mihna for refusing to say that the Qur’an was created?
explanation: Under the Abbasid caliph al-Mamun and his successors Ahmad bin Hanbal endured persecution but did not yield.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which scholar is known as “Hujjat-ul-Islam” and wrote Ihya Ulum-ud-Din?
explanation: Abu Hamid al-Ghazali, who taught at the Nizamiyyah of Baghdad, earned the title Hujjat-ul-Islam (Proof of Islam).

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Who translated the Holy Qur’an into Persian in eighteenth-century Delhi?
explanation: Shah Waliullah’s Persian translation, Fath-ur-Rahman, brought the meaning of the Qur’an to ordinary educated Muslims of India.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Who is known as Mujaddid Alf Sani?
explanation: Sheikh Ahmad Sirhindi resisted Akbar’s Din-e-Ilahi and is called the Reviver of the Second Millennium.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Kashf-ul-Mahjub, an early Persian treatise on Sufism, was written by:
explanation: Ali bin Usman Hujwiri, buried in Lahore, wrote Kashf-ul-Mahjub, the oldest Persian work on Sufism.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Khawaja Moinuddin Chishti preached Islam in the Subcontinent from:
explanation: Khawaja Moinuddin Chishti settled in Ajmer, where his shrine stands, and spread the Chishti order in India.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Qadiriyyah Sufi order is named after:
explanation: Sheikh Abdul Qadir Jilani of Baghdad is regarded as the founder of the Qadiriyyah order.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Rabia Basri is remembered in Islamic history as:
o: A poet of the Abbasid court
A woman saint known for pure love of Allah
A narrator of the Charter of Madinah
explanation: Rabia of Basra, an eighth-century mystic, taught that Allah should be worshipped out of love, not fear or hope of reward.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Masnavi, a celebrated Persian spiritual poem, was written by:
explanation: Rumi’s Masnavi-e-Ma’navi, composed in Konya, is one of the most influential works of Islamic mysticism.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The earliest comprehensive biography of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), later edited by Ibn Hisham, was compiled by:
explanation: Muhammad ibn Ishaq’s Sirat Rasool Allah survives mainly through Ibn Hisham’s edition, the standard early Seerah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Spain was conquered for the Muslims in 711 CE by:
o: Musa bin Nusair’s son Abdul Aziz
explanation: Tariq bin Ziyad crossed from North Africa at the rock later named Jabal-ut-Tariq (Gibraltar) and defeated King Roderick.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Sindh was conquered by Muhammad bin Qasim in:
explanation: Muhammad bin Qasim defeated Raja Dahir in 712 CE, bringing Islam to Sindh and Multan.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Jerusalem was recovered from the Crusaders in 1187 by:
explanation: After his victory at Hattin, Salahuddin Ayyubi took Jerusalem and was noted for his humane treatment of its Christians.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Uthman (RA) is called “Ghani” because of his:
o: Great generosity in spending his wealth for Islam
explanation: He spent lavishly for the Muslims, for example buying the well of Rumah and equipping the army of Tabuk.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The first person to accept Islam was:
explanation: Khadijah believed in the Prophet as soon as he told her of the first revelation.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Among free adult men, the first to accept Islam was:
explanation: Abu Bakr accepted Islam at once and brought several future members of the Ashara Mubashara to Islam.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The kunyah of Hazrat Umar (RA) was:
explanation: Umar was known as Abu Hafs; Al-Farooq was his title.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which Companion was the first to recite the Qur’an aloud publicly near the Ka’bah in Makkah?
explanation: Ibn Masud recited Surah Ar-Rahman before the Quraysh gathered at the Ka’bah and was beaten for it.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which Prophet was the brother and helper of Hazrat Musa (AS)?
explanation: Musa (AS) prayed that his brother Harun be made his helper, and Allah granted Harun prophethood.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: According to the Qur’an, the Ark of Hazrat Nuh (AS) came to rest on:
explanation: Surah Hud states that after the flood the Ark settled on al-Judi.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) was chosen as caliph at:
explanation: The Ansar and Muhajirin met at the Saqifah (hall) of Banu Sa’idah, where Abu Bakr received the first pledge; a general pledge followed in the mosque.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) was officially styled:
explanation: He was called Khalifah of the Messenger of Allah; the title Amir-ul-Momineen came into regular use with Umar.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: In his first address as caliph, Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) told the people to:
o: Obey him in all matters without question
Obey him only as long as he obeyed Allah and His Messenger
Pay a special tax for the army
Leave all decisions to the Ansar
explanation: He asked them to help him when right and correct him when wrong, making the ruler’s authority conditional on obedience to Allah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The wars fought in the caliphate of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) against apostates and false claimants of prophethood are called:
explanation: Riddah means apostasy; Abu Bakr suppressed the revolts that broke out after the Prophet’s death and restored unity.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) fought the tribes that refused to pay Zakat because he held that:
o: Zakat had been abolished after the Prophet
Zakat cannot be separated from Salah
explanation: He declared he would fight anyone who separated Salah from Zakat, treating the state’s collection of Zakat as part of the religion.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The false prophet Musaylimah was defeated at the Battle of:
explanation: Khalid bin Walid defeated Musaylimah at Yamamah in 11–12 AH, where many memorisers of the Qur’an were martyred.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Battle of Zat-us-Salasil (Battle of Chains), in Hazrat Abu Bakr’s caliphate, was fought against the:
explanation: Khalid bin Walid defeated the Sasanian Persians in Iraq; the name comes from the chains their soldiers used to prevent retreat.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Battle of Ajnadayn, fought in Hazrat Abu Bakr’s caliphate, was against the:
explanation: Ajnadayn in Palestine (13 AH) was the first major victory over the Byzantines, opening the way to Syria.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Before his death, Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) nominated as his successor, after consulting senior Companions:
explanation: Abu Bakr consulted leading Companions and then nominated Umar, whom the people accepted by pledge.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Before his death, Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) directed that the allowance he had taken from the Bait-ul-Mal should be:
explanation: He arranged for what he had drawn as caliph to be returned from his own property, setting a standard of honesty with public funds.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) passed away in:
explanation: His caliphate lasted a little over two years, from 11 AH to 13 AH.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Abu Bakr’s instructions to his armies prohibited them from:
o: Killing women, children and the elderly
explanation: He forbade harming non-combatants, monks, fruit trees and animals, codifying the Prophet’s ethics of war.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The first caliph to be addressed as “Amir-ul-Momineen” was:
explanation: Since “Khalifah of the Khalifah of the Messenger” was cumbersome, Umar came to be called Amir-ul-Momineen, Commander of the Faithful.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Hijri calendar was introduced during the caliphate of:
explanation: Umar adopted a calendar dated from the Hijrah to regularise official correspondence and records.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The first month of the Hijri calendar is:
explanation: Although the Hijrah took place in Rabi-ul-Awwal, Muharram was fixed as the first month of the Islamic year.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which Caliph introduced the Diwan system of state registers?
explanation: Umar set up registers (Diwan) listing soldiers and citizens entitled to stipends, the basis of an organised administration.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Umar (RA) strengthened the justice system by:
o: Appointing Qazis independent of provincial governors
Letting tribal chiefs decide all cases
explanation: He appointed judges such as Qazi Shuraih separately from governors, an early separation of the judiciary from the executive.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Qazi Shuraih, one of the most famous judges of early Islam, was appointed by Hazrat Umar (RA) as Qazi of:
explanation: Shuraih served as judge of Kufa for decades, from Umar’s time onwards.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The garrison cities of Kufa and Basra were founded during the caliphate of:
explanation: Both cities were built in Iraq under Umar as military cantonments (amsar) that grew into major centres.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Fustat, the first Muslim capital of Egypt, was founded by:
explanation: After conquering Egypt in Umar’s caliphate, Amr bin al-As founded Fustat, near present-day Cairo.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Jerusalem surrendered peacefully and its keys were handed over to:
explanation: The Patriarch Sophronius insisted on surrendering to the caliph himself, so Umar travelled to Jerusalem in about 16 AH.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The covenant given by Hazrat Umar (RA) to the people of Jerusalem guaranteed them:
o: Safety of their lives, property and churches
Seats in the Shura of Madinah
explanation: Umar’s guarantee (Al-Uhdah al-Umariyyah) protected the Christians’ persons, property and places of worship.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Battle of Yarmuk was fought between the Muslims and the:
explanation: At Yarmuk (15 AH/636 CE) the Muslims decisively defeated the Byzantine army, securing Syria.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Muslim army at the Battle of Qadisiyyah against the Persians was commanded by:
explanation: Sa’d bin Abi Waqqas led the Muslims to victory at Qadisiyyah, which broke Sasanian power in Iraq.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which Sasanian capital was captured by the Muslims after Qadisiyyah?
explanation: Sa’d bin Abi Waqqas occupied the Persian capital Mada’in (Ctesiphon) on the Tigris in Umar’s caliphate.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which battle is called “Fath-ul-Futuh” (the victory of victories)?
explanation: Nahawand (21 AH) destroyed the last major Sasanian army, opening all of Persia to the Muslims.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Egypt was conquered in the caliphate of Hazrat Umar (RA) by:
explanation: Amr bin al-As led the campaign that took Egypt from the Byzantines, including Alexandria.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Umar (RA) removed Hazrat Khalid bin Walid (RA) from supreme command mainly so that:
o: People would not think victory depended on Khalid rather than Allah
explanation: Umar explained that he feared people were placing their trust in Khalid; Khalid continued to serve loyally under Abu Ubaidah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Aam-ur-Ramadah (the Year of Ashes) in Hazrat Umar’s caliphate refers to:
explanation: In 18 AH drought and famine struck Arabia; Umar organised relief from Egypt, Syria and Iraq and ate only coarse food until it ended.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: During the famine of Aam-ur-Ramadah, Hazrat Umar (RA) suspended:
o: The punishment of cutting the hand for theft
The collection of Jizyah from Christians
explanation: Because hunger could drive people to steal, he did not apply the hadd of theft during the famine, showing that doubt averts fixed penalties.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The plague of Amwas, which killed several leading Companions in Syria, occurred in the caliphate of:
explanation: The plague struck in 18 AH; Umar turned back from his journey to Syria after consultation.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Umar (RA) extended state stipends from the Bait-ul-Mal even to:
explanation: He first paid allowances for weaned children, then from birth, so that mothers would not wean infants early.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Umar (RA) decided that the conquered farmland of Iraq should:
o: Remain with its cultivators, subject to Kharaj, for the benefit of the state
explanation: After consultation he kept the Sawad lands as a public resource taxed through Kharaj, providing revenue for future generations.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Before his death, Hazrat Umar (RA) left the choice of his successor to:
o: A council of six senior Companions
explanation: He named six of the Ashara Mubashara as an electoral council to choose one of themselves within three days.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Umar (RA) was fatally stabbed while leading the Fajr prayer by:
explanation: Abu Lu’lu’ah, a Persian slave, attacked him in the mosque in 23 AH.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The consultation that led to the election of Hazrat Uthman (RA) was conducted by:
explanation: Abdur Rahman bin Auf withdrew his own candidacy and consulted the council and the people before pledging to Uthman.
